title: fix(app-shell): Studio shows labels first, machine names and ids as secondary text (objectui#11862)
body:
Refs #11862 (sites 1 to 3 and the nav editor's edit-mode cards land wherever the label is already in hand; the remainder is every draft-only label, objectstack-ai/objectstack#22200, and the Changes list, whose file is on objectui#11807's claim: see "The remainder")
Clause-②: no

Studio shows a label as the primary text, and the machine name or id as secondary text (smaller, monospace), on the maintainer's word 「所有地方以标签为主，机器名只作为次要信息」. Display only: nothing that is saved changes, no label is written where the author typed none, and nav item ids are minted as before. No export, prop, `@object-ui/types` member or accepted input changes.

## What changed

- **Explain access, the Principal line** (`AccessExplainPanel`). The line printed `decision.principal.userId` and `onBehalfOf.userId` raw. Each id now reads as the user's name and email, with the id beneath it as secondary text. The name comes from the row the user picker handed back (no second lookup), or else from the lookup the picker itself reads: one `find('sys_user', { $filter: { id: { $in: ids } } })` through the same data adapter, once per explain run, only for ids not already known. An id the lookup cannot answer (no row, or the read fails) reads as the id, as before.
- **Access pillar, the permission-set list** (`AccessPillar`'s rail). Each set shows its label, with its machine name beneath it. A set without a label reads as its name alone.
- **Interfaces nav rail** (`NavTree`). Each leaf shows its label (authored, or what it inherits through the objectui#11196 resolver), with the machine name of what it opens beneath it. A leaf that names no target yet ("Add nav item" left unbound, which the editor keeps in its place) reads as the editor's existing untitled wording, "Item N" by its place (`engine.appNav.item`), never as its minted `nav_item_N` id. "Names no target" is the save's own rule, `navPayloadOf`, not a second copy of it.
- **Nav-item inspector** (`StudioNavItemInspector`). It has no title; the one place it names the entry is the Label field's placeholder, which read `nav_item_N` for an unbound entry. It now offers the same "Item N" wording.
- **The nav editor's edit-mode cards** (`AppNavCanvas`'s `navLabel`; the canvas also serves the app designer's navigation editor). A card for an entry with no label that names no target yet read the `nav_item_N` id the canvas minted. It now reads the same positional "Item N" wording by its place (「导航项 N」 in Chinese), and a card click titles the selection the same way. "Names no target" is the module's own `namesNoTarget`, the rule its save uses. A bound entry, an authored label and a label-less group (the runtime names it by its id, and it is saved) read as before. `addItem` is untouched: ids are minted as before and no label is written. Added in a second round, after the seat amended the claim (comment 6053526025).
- One module-private `StudioNameLabel` in `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` draws the label-plus-name shape for the two Studio lists. Measured first: Studio had no shared label-plus-name component, only the inline idiom the package switcher and `BuilderLanding` use (`block truncate font-mono text-[10px] text-muted-foreground`), which this matches. The secondary name is `aria-hidden`, so each row's accessible name stays the label it was (the nav rail still carries `type · name` on its `title`). The Principal line has its own small `PrincipalPerson` in `AccessExplainPanel.tsx`, because a person is a name, an email and an id.

## Measured: the dispatch's mechanism hypotheses

- **H1, true for published rows, false for draft-only rows.** The permission-set rail and the nav rail render from published rows that carry a `label`, and those now lead. A row that exists only as a draft is listed from the `_drafts` header, which carries `type`, `name`, `organizationId`, `packageId`, `updatedAt` and `updatedBy`, and no label (objectstack `listDrafts` in `metadata-protocol`, and the client's `MetadataDraftHeader`). The issue's own examples are such rows: `technician` (a set just created as a draft) and `repairs_repair_ticket` (a draft-only object, objectui#11843's measured instance). For those rows no label is in hand anywhere on the surface, so they still read as their name.
- **H2, true.** `navEntryLabelText` with `useNavTargetLabel` gives the entry's authored label, else its target's current label from the console's metadata, else the target's machine name, else the entry's `id`. `NavTree` did not bypass it. `nav_item_N` came from that last rung, for an entry with no target; `repairs_repair_tick…` came from the machine-name rung, because a draft-only object is not in the console's metadata.
- **H3, true, and the list is not where the dispatch placed it.** The Changes list is `DraftChangesPanel` in `packages/app-shell/src/preview/`, not in `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` (the cited spot there is the `Changes · N` count button). Its entries come from the `_drafts` header and carry no label. Inside the panel, labels in hand without a new request: the published list it already reads per type to classify NEW and UPDATE (`publishedNamesOf` keeps only the names), and the object draft bodies the security-posture lint reads. A NEW non-object draft has no label in hand.

## The remainder (seat ruling 6053526025)

- **Draft-only labels** at the two rails and the Changes list: ruled at the producer, objectstack-ai/objectstack#22200 (the `_drafts` header carries the row's `label`; the repository's `listDrafts` already reads the whole row and drops the body). objectui adds no per-surface read for a label in the meantime, and the draft-only rows stay pinned here as the "no label in hand" controls.
- **The Changes list** (`preview/DraftChangesPanel.tsx`): not this PR. The file is on the in-flight claim for objectui#11807. Its UPDATE entries could lead with the published label it already reads per type; its NEW entries wait on objectstack-ai/objectstack#22200.

## Tests

All on head `386bb41` (the branch after a merge of `main` at `09821b1`), in one verify-lock hold:

- `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter="@object-ui/app-shell^..." --concurrency=2` → exit 0, 28 of 28 tasks.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) → exit 0; `--listFilesOnly` shows the four new pin files in the test program.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/AccessExplainPanel packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/ packages/app-shell/src/views/viewCacheInvalidation.guard.test.tsx apps/console/src/components/StudioRoute` → 240 files, 2221 tests passed.
- New pins: `AccessExplainPanel.principalPerson-11862.test.tsx` (5), `StudioDesignSurface.accessRailLabels-11862.test.tsx` (3), `StudioDesignSurface.navRailLabels-11862.test.tsx` (6), `AppNavCanvas.untitledCard-11862.test.tsx` (7: an unbound and an untyped entry read "Item N", in English and 「导航项 N」 in Chinese, and a click titles the selection so; controls: a bound entry, an authored label, a label-less group).
- Existing pins that change on the ruling, each from `nav_item_N` to the positional wording: `navItemInspectorLabel-11196` (the placeholder), `AppNavCanvas.labelLessBirth-11196` (the card and the new entry's selection title), `AppNavCanvas.navPayload-11776` (finds the unbound card by its text), `StudioDesignSurface.navPlaceholderSave-11776` and `StudioDesignSurface.navItemTypes-11790` (the edit rail's text). Two suites (`accessGuard`, `pillarNavGuard`) asked the whole screen for `set_a`, which the rail now also shows as secondary text; they now ask the pillar's main panel.
- Reverse checks, one per site, each through `ablation-replace.mjs` with the fix committed, red and green counts written down before the run, and the restore proven (blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty):
  - the Principal line without the resolved person: 2 red, 3 green, as predicted;
  - the permission-set row back to the bare label: 1 red, 2 green, as predicted;
  - the nav row back to the bare label: 3 red, 3 green, as predicted;
  - the inspector placeholder back to the inherited text: 2 red, 12 green, as predicted;
  - `navLabel` without its no-target line: 8 red (the four new card pins, the two `labelLessBirth` pins, the two `navPayload` keyboard cases), 40 green, as predicted.
- Gates, exit 0: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`, and `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`. `check:i18n-designer-parity` does not apply: no row was added.
- Lint, narrowed to the 14 touched source files (the repo-wide run is CI's): ESLint as the package's `lint` script runs it, 0 errors, and the same per-file warning counts as the merge base. The config enables no type-aware linting and no rule in `eslint-rules/` reads another file, so this diff cannot move another file's verdict.

## Acceptance notes

- The nav-item inspector's object picker writes each option as "label (name)", so an object whose label is its name reads `repairs_repair_ticket (repairs_repair_ticket)`. The nearby pickers (`optionsOf`, the Explain access object dropdown) skip the parenthesis when the two are equal. Noted, not filed; it is a polish item.
